newsitem.title: USA: Counties urge US partnership in power deregulation.
newsitem.headline: Counties urge US partnership in power deregulation.

text.p: National Association of Counties' board of directors this weekend said that state and local governments must be "partners" in any national plan to restructure the nation's electric industry.

The board, meeting in Baltimore this week for the group's 62nd annual conference, adopted a 13-part resolution on the issue at a session Sunday. The 3,400 delegates attending the conference will take a final vote on the resolution Tuesday.
"The electric utility industry is being restructured on the federal and state levels from one that is highly regulated to one in which there is significant competition," the board's resolution says.
The following are some of the 13 principles backed by NACo's board:
* Customer Choice: state, not federal, legislators should determine whether electricity customers should be allowed to select the electric power supplier of their choice;
* Consultation: state and local government leaders must be partners in any national restructuring plan;
* Transition: counties need enough time to adjust to new structures, avoid service disruptions, and adjust to possible tax revenue changes resulting from restructuring;
* Revenue Authority: counties should continue to have the authority to issue franchises and/or taxes; no federal or state action should preempt or interfere with county revenue authority;
* Rights-of-way: counties must retain full authority over their own rights-of-ways and over recovery costs for their use;
* County and Municipal Facilities: restructuring must not affect counties' ability to form utilities in the future; the costs of forming utilities should not be shifted to other counties;
* Aggregation: under any restructuring, counties should have the opportunity to combine electric loads of various users and to negotiate purchase of elecricity on behalf of those consumers.
